title: Probability the special coordinate is a fixed intersecting index
statement: Equip the finite space of hard samples with the uniform probability measure, where each sample consists of a special coordinate $T \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, two Boolean bits $x_T$ and $y_T$, and a value in $\{\text{neither},\text{leftOnly},\text{rightOnly}\}$ for every one of the $n$ coordinates. Then for each fixed coordinate $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, the probability that the special coordinate equals $i$ and that both special bits are true, that is $T = i$ and $x_T = y_T = \text{true}$, is exactly $\dfrac{1}{4n}$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
i is a fixed coordinate in Fin n
uniform probability measure on the finite sample space of hard samples
event: special coordinate T equals i
event: both special bits x_T and y_T are true
replaced: Under the hard distribution, $T=i$ and the special bits intersect with probability $1/(4n)$.
